questions.key_step: Eliminate to solve the 3x3 system, get lambda from eq 4, then point-plane distance
questions.justification: Three routine stages (elimination, lambda, distance formula), nothing non-standard; options available.

questions.key_step: Expand the squares and use AA^T=I (noncommuting terms cancel)
questions.justification: Short expansion where A A^T = I is used twice; routine but needs care with order of products.

questions.key_step: Row operation R2-2R1 makes the determinant independent of r and n
questions.justification: One familiar determinant trick applied once; the answer is then read off.

questions.key_step: Reduce A^5 repeatedly using A^3 = 2A^2+4A-4I
questions.justification: Routine repeated substitution of the matrix polynomial; two reductions, standard idea.

questions.key_step: Expand determinant to 2a^2+6a+1=0 and locate roots in an interval
questions.justification: Determinant expansion plus quadratic-root location; several routine steps, no insight.

questions.key_step: Telescope the recurrence to A^50 = 25A^2-24I
questions.justification: Spotting the telescoping sum is the one idea; then one matrix square and a sum of entries.

questions.key_step: (sqrt3+sqrt2)(sqrt3-sqrt2)=1 so t+1/t=10
questions.justification: One familiar reciprocal-pair move, then a quadratic.

questions.key_step: Write the three terms as 12-d,12,12+d and solve the ratio equation for d
questions.justification: Longer algebra chain (two sets, products, a quadratic) but each step standard; options help.

questions.key_step: Telescoping S_2025 and AP sum to get p
questions.justification: Two standard ideas chained (telescoping, AP sum) with simple numbers.

questions.key_step: Zero determinant then cos(2a+pi/4)=-1/2 within (0,pi/2)
questions.justification: Determinant expansion followed by a trig equation with a domain check.

questions.key_step: Compare exponents: r^10=r1^(p-1) with r^2=r1^4
questions.justification: Single familiar GP manipulation.

questions.key_step: Use sum condition to get a and d, then m, then the 2m-term sum
questions.justification: Several AP-sum steps chained; routine.

questions.key_step: Symmetric functions give alpha^4+beta^4=98 and (alpha^6+beta^6)/10=97
questions.justification: Two power-sum computations then new equation; routine chain with surds.

questions.key_step: sqrt(x)=t turns each bracket into a quadratic
questions.justification: One substitution used twice; solutions all distinct.

questions.key_step: Discriminant 16+4n perfect square; count squares in [24,104]
questions.justification: Short chain with a careful count of squares in a range.

questions.key_step: Cofactor equations give alpha=2,beta=1; det(AB)=det(A)*det(B), det(B)=det(A)^2
questions.justification: Cofactor matrix (not adjoint) handling and the det(cof)=det^(n-1) fact; slip-prone, a little beyond routine.

questions.key_step: Newton recurrence P_{n+2}=sqrt2 P_{n+1}+sqrt3 P_n reduces the long expression
questions.justification: Surd-heavy algebra with a recurrence applied twice; precision risk, no options to shortcut the grind.

questions.key_step: AM condition gives r^2+r-2=0, reject r=1, then S20-S18=a19+a20
questions.justification: Standard GP chain with a rejection step.

questions.key_step: Odd-indexed AP sum gives a1=-5d, then n from sum zero
questions.justification: Two AP sums; routine.

questions.key_step: Two AP conditions on a-2,ar-7,ar^2-9,ar^3-5; divide to get r=2
questions.justification: Setting up and dividing two cubic-in-r relations is a non-obvious elimination; precision risk.
